kurals.tr: Naanalam Ennum Nalanutaimai Annalam / Yaanalaththu Ulladhooum Andru
kurals.m: The possession of that goodness which is called the goodness of speech is (even to others) better than any other goodness

kurals.tr: Aakkamung Ketum Adhanaal Varudhalaal / Kaaththompal Sollinkat Sorvu
kurals.m: Since (both) wealth and evil result from (their) speech, ministers should most carefully guard themselves against faultiness therein

kurals.tr: Kettaarp Pinikkum Thakaiyavaaik Kelaarum / Vetpa Mozhivadhaam Sol
kurals.m: The (minister's) speech is that which seeks (to express) elements as bind his friends (to himself) and is so delivered as to make even his enemies desire (his friendship)

kurals.tr: Thiranarindhu Solluka Sollai Aranum / Porulum Adhaninooungu Il
kurals.m: Understand the qualities (of your hearers) and (then) make your speech; for superior to it, there is neither virtue nor wealth

kurals.tr: Solluka Sollaip Piridhorsol Achchollai / Vellunjol Inmai Arindhu
kurals.m: Deliver your speech, after assuring yourself that no counter speech can defeat your own

kurals.tr: Vetpaththaanj Chollip Pirarsol Payankotal / Maatchiyin Maasatraar Kol
kurals.m: It is the opinion of those who are free from defects in diplomacy that the minister should speak so as to make his hearers desire (to hear more) and grasp the meaning of what he hears himself

kurals.tr: Solalvallan Sorvilan Anjaan Avanai / Ikalvellal Yaarkkum Aridhu
kurals.m: It is impossible for any one to conquer him by intrique who possesses power of speech, and is neither faulty nor timid

kurals.tr: Viraindhu Thozhilketkum Gnaalam Nirandhinidhu / Solludhal Vallaarp Perin
kurals.m: If there be those who can speak on various subjects in their proper order and in a pleasing manner, the world would readily accept them

kurals.tr: Palasollak Kaamuruvar Mandramaa Satra / Silasollal Thetraa Thavar
kurals.m: They will desire to utter many words, who do not know how to speak a few faultless ones

kurals.tr: Inaruzhththum Naaraa Malaranaiyar Katradhu / Unara Viriththuraiyaa Thaar
kurals.m: Those who are unable to set forth their acquirements (before others) are like flowers blossoming in a cluster and yet without fragrance
